title: Financial Assistance Program (Charity Care) — Schedule of Discounts by Household Poverty Band
content:
## Schedule of discounts

Under the Financial Assistance Program (Charity Care), each award tier applies to a band of household FPL percent (one decimal) and carries one percent discount on the FAP charge basis of an eligible encounter. The band floor is the household FPL percent at or above which the tier applies; the band ceiling is the household FPL percent at or below which the tier applies, and for the presumptive tier it is the presumed ceiling. The discount is 0 for medical hardship, which is cap-based.

| Tier | Band floor (FPL %) | Band ceiling (FPL %) | Discount on the FAP charge basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Riverbend Presumptive Charity Care | 0.0 | 200.0 (presumed) | 100.0 percent |
| Riverbend Full Charity Care (0-200% FPL) | 0.0 | 200.0 | 100.0 percent |
| Riverbend 80% Charity Discount (201-250% FPL) | 200.1 | 250.0 | 80.0 percent |
| Riverbend 60% Charity Discount (251-300% FPL) | 250.1 | 300.0 | 60.0 percent |
| Riverbend 40% Charity Discount (301-400% FPL) | 300.1 | 400.0 | 40.0 percent |
| Riverbend Medical Hardship Assistance (above 400% FPL) | 400.1 | 600.0 | 0.0 percent (cap-based) |

### Reading the schedule

- Both bounds of a band are inclusive, and household FPL percent is carried to one decimal, so the bands meet without a gap: a household at 200.0 percent sits in the 0-200 band, and one at 200.1 percent sits in the 201-250 band.
- A hypothetical household screened at 250.0 percent falls in the 80% Charity Discount band; at 250.1 percent it falls in the 60% Charity Discount band.
- The 0.0 percent figure on the Medical Hardship tier is not a refusal of assistance: that tier limits the patient's liability by a cap instead of a percent discount.
